description: Manual corrections for the elementary flows of GreenDelta's openLCA LCIA methods 2.8.2 package, applied to the extracted records before anything reads them. Matched on name where the correction is about the substance, as the other lists' files are: GreenDelta repeats a substance once per compartment, so a rule keyed on one row would miss the next compartment added.

fixes.comment: 7727-37-9 is dinitrogen -- N2, the inert gas that is 78% of the air, indexed by Common Chemistry as `Nitrogen` with structure `N#N`. `Nitrogen, organic bound` is not a compound: it is the nitrogen locked inside the organic matter of a discharge, reported as a mass of nitrogen, and no registry number can name it because a number names one compound and this is a measurement over many. GreenDelta writes the gas's number on all eleven of its organic-bound rows, one per water compartment, exactly as ecoinvent does on its five and EF 3.1 on its five, so the number has to come off here too or the merge is handed lists that disagree about whether a nutrient load is nitrogen gas (#26). Removed rather than corrected: there is nothing to correct it to, and with it gone the rows group by name, onto the same flow object EF's do. GreenDelta's own `Nitrogen` rows keep the number, which is theirs. The reasoning and the evidence are in ef-3.1-manual-fixes.json. Matched on name rather than UUID for the reason given in the description above. (#57)

`dinitrogen` names the gas, and this flow is not the gas -- same argument as the registry number above. GreenDelta carries it on five of the eleven organic-bound rows, as ecoinvent does from 3.9.1 on. A synonym is what the label rules and the name index read, so leaving it would re-assert by name the identity the registry-number removal takes away. (#57)
The second of the two gas synonyms on the organic-bound rows. Removed for the same reason as `dinitrogen` above. (#57)

The package's `Stibnite` in `Resource / in ground` is ecoinvent's row under ecoinvent's own uuid, carrying ecoinvent's number: 1345-04-6, which IARC (vol. 47) gives to manufactured antimony trisulfide, where 1317-86-8 is the mineral. ecoinvent's fixes rewrite it to 1317-86-8 in every release, with the evidence set out there -- every list's stibnite is a resource out of the ground, every row for the compound is an emission (EF 3.1's thirteen), and BAFU registers its stibnite 1317-86-8 independently (#123). Copied here so the package's copy of the row reaches the mineral the other lists' copies reach rather than joining EF's antimony trisulfide, which is where the uncorrected number sent it on the build of 20 October 2026 (#412). Matched on the uuid and the name together, so a release that reuses the uuid for something else is not rewritten.

The synonym the package writes on five of its six `Epoxiconazole` rows registered 135319-73-2, restored on the agricultural-soil row that ships without it -- the same correction ecoinvent's fixes make for the two rows of its own eight that lack it. The number is ecoinvent's, stereochemistry unspecified, and EF 3.1 registers the fungicide 106325-08-0 under BASF's development code `Bas 480f`; neither list carries the other's number, so the synonym is the only bridge, and without it this row minted a second `Epoxiconazole` on the build of 20 October 2026 while its siblings reached EF's (#412, and see 0826).

The package writes 2356-62-9 on its four rows named for HFE-236ea2, and that number is HFE-227ea's: EF 3.1 registers `HFE-227EA` (trifluoromethyl 1,2,2,2-tetrafluoroethyl ether, C3HF7O) under 2356-62-9 and `HFE-236ea2` (1,2,2-trifluoroethyl trifluoromethyl ether, C3H2F6O) under 84011-06-3, and Stepwise 2006 writes 84011-06-3 on its row of this exact name. The name says which molecule GreenDelta meant twice over, in words and in the designation, and the number contradicts it. Rewritten to the name's number: on the build of 20 October 2026 the four rows reached `HFE-227EA`, and GreenDelta's two different factors for one flow and place were reported as eight collisions (#412). Matched on the name and the wrong number together, so a release that corrects the number itself is left alone.

The package writes 61805-96-7 on all fourteen of its `Arsenic V` rows, and the number names no arsenic compound: Common Chemistry does not resolve it, and PubChem lists it only as a second registry number on 1,3-dimethylthiourea (CID 2723631), a sulfur compound with no arsenic in it. The name is EF 3.1's `arsenic (v)`, registered 17428-41-0 and published here as `Arsenic(5+)`, and `lcia-substance-decisions.json` already reads GreenDelta's `Arsenic V` as that substance for the factor it states. Rewritten to that number: with the unresolvable one, the fourteen rows minted a second `Arsenic(5+)` on the build of 20 October 2026, because `Arsenic V` is an alternative label on a substance that carries a registry number and the name route refuses such a hit (#412). Matched on the name and the number together.

`HG-02` is an industry designation for a hydrofluoropolyether, 1,1'-oxybis[2-(difluoromethoxy)-1,1,2,2-tetrafluoroethane], registered 205367-61-9. EF 3.1 shipped its flow under this designation with no number, and `ef-3.1-manual-fixes.json` renames it to the systematic name and keeps `HG-02` as a synonym; the package copies the designation as its own flow with no number either. The package's factors say which molecule it is -- EF 3.1 (adapted) `Climate change` 5,730, IPCC 2013 GWP 100a 2,730, the numbers EF and IPCC give HG-02 -- so the number is written on. On the first full build that merged the list (20 October 2026, merge run `76b3ec8f`) the row minted a second substance named `HG-02` beside the ether, because the designation is an alternative label on a substance that carries a number and the name route refuses such a hit (#412).

Tribromomethane is bromoform, CHBr3, 75-25-2, which EF 3.1 publishes as `Bromoform` in thirteen compartments and the package itself ships twenty times under that name with the number. This one row carries the systematic name and no number; its factors are bromoform's (EF 3.1 (adapted) and IPCC 2021 GWP 100 both 0.25). On the first full build that merged the list (20 October 2026, merge run `76b3ec8f`) it minted a second substance, `Tribromomethane`, beside bromoform (#412).

match.name: Helium, in natural gas, in ground

fixes.comment: ecoinvent's `Helium, in natural gas` under ecoinvent's uuid, helium as a resource in the ground, which ecoinvent's correspondence table sends to EF's helium and which the package copies with the number left off; Ecological Scarcity 2013 scores it as a mineral resource. The package's four other helium rows carry 7440-59-7 and reach `Helium`. On the first full build that merged the list (20 October 2026, merge run `76b3ec8f`) this one minted `Helium, In Natural Gas, In Ground` as a substance of its own (#412).

Liquid water is published in cubic metres throughout this list -- every flow carrying EF 3.1's `Water use` factors, every water resource ecoinvent ships -- and BAFU's sixteen kilogram water rows were rewritten to cubic metres at 0.001 m3/kg in `bafu-2026-v1-manual-fixes.json` (#78, 0409). The package measures 52 of its kept water rows by mass, under 33 names, beside cubic-metre rows of the same kinds of water; a kilogram row landing on a cubic-metre flow is a unit crossing, and one landing where no flow exists yet mints a kilogram flow, which is what `Waste water` did on the first full build that merged the list (20 October 2026, merge run `76b3ec8f`). The same density, 0.001, for every one of them, sea water included, as BAFU's were. The conversion is published on the row's concept association, so a factor the package states per kilogram for the row is converted by the same number.

The conversion is published on the row's concept association, so a factor the package states per kilogram for the row is converted by the same number.

`Propane, dibromopentafluoro-` is EF 3.1's `Dibromopentafluoropropane`, 431-78-7. One of six rows the package ships under Stepwise 2006's SimaPro spelling -- the parent in front, the substituents after the comma -- with no registry number. Stepwise's rows of these exact names reach EF 3.1's substances through the SimaPro name rewriting that runs for SimaPro-shaped lists only (#285), and a package that copies the spelling without the number gets neither, so on the six-list build of 20 October 2026 with the first corrections (merge run `0c16f168`) each minted a substance of its own under the SimaPro name, which the read-only lookup then chose for Stepwise's rows. The number is the one Stepwise's row reaches EF's substance under; the package's own factor on the row is that substance's GWP.

No other list ships `Energy, from hydrogen`, and the package files it twice: `Resource / unspecified` and `Resource / in water`, neither with a factor in any EF 3.1 category. On the six-list build of 22 October 2026 (commit 5a343f5) that minted the substance in two places, `Resource → Ground` (where this list reads the package's unspecified resources) and `Resource → Water`. The energy content of hydrogen is not drawn from a water body, so this row is filed in the ground, where its sibling is read. Filed `in ground` rather than `unspecified`: the package's unspecified resources are each read by a rule of their own (#381), and a row moved into that compartment has none.

17428-41-0 is arsenate's number, arsenic(V), and the row is the generic arsenic ion with the charge unstated, the reading AGRIBALYSE's `Arsenic, ion` fix in agribalyse-3.2-manual-fixes.json makes. The package writes it on 16 of its `Arsenic ion` rows, and where EF states one their factors are the element's, not arsenate's: 1,725.9 for freshwater ecotoxicity in agricultural soil, which is EF's `Arsenic`, where `Arsenic(5+)` is 2,506.95. The package's other 26 `Arsenic ion` emissions, which carry the element's number or none, already reach `Arsenic, ion`; these 16 reached `Arsenic(5+)` by the number, beside the package's `Arsenic V` rows, and GreenDelta's two numbers collided there (six-list build of 24 October 2026, commit 34984fd, 6 collisions). Removed rather than replaced: no number names a generic ion. Matched on the name and the number together, so a release that drops the number leaves nothing to do. (#439)
